title: Choose the visual world for SYSTEM // SELF (round 2)
question: The roll assigned the Metro Line. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Metro Line
options.lineage: Delhi Metro line maps and station signage
options.thesis: Your progress is a metro map: each domain is a coloured line, ranks E to S are stations, you are the train between them.
options.viewport: Today: a five-line metro diagram with your marker between station E and D on each line, the briefing as a platform announcement, quests as next stops, labeled nav bar.
options.risk: The map can become decoration if the lines don't carry real distances; dense lists still need plain rows.

raised.raise: The one bright accent appears only on things you can press; everything else stays line colour or neutral.
Rules and ticks are 1px hairlines, and the palette works in three values besides the line colours.
Rank of text is carried by weight and case, not by more sizes: three sizes total.
Today is a fixed budget: quests show how much of the day's time they take and must fit it.

options.label: Broadcast Scorecard
options.thesis: Your day as a live match: a score bug, a required run rate to the next rank, player-card stats per domain.
options.viewport: Today: a slanted live score bug (Rank E, 23.4, need 2.6 in 14 days), five domain player cards, quests as the next overs.
options.risk: Familiar sports-broadcast look many apps borrow; can get loud and busy.

options.label: Departure Board
options.thesis: Rivals and quests as rows on a departure board; when someone passes you, the row flips.
options.viewport: Today: a board of quests as departures (time, destination, domain, status), delayed rows amber, refused rows dim red.
options.case: Great for rivals and quest status; less personal for the rank and stats.
options.risk: Everything becomes a table; can feel like transit, not self.

options.label: Pulse Plot
options.thesis: Matte black, and your last 30 days drawn as a stack of white pulse lines; the gap is visible as a shape.
options.viewport: Today: a white-line pulse plot of 30 days owns the top half, a colour-code strip for domains, quests below in small engraved caps.
options.case: The strongest picture of 'the gap', but less obvious to a first-time user.
options.risk: Art-school cool can hide the task; the plot must stay readable.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards on a warm ground, friendly labels.
options.case: Loses both axes: the PRD's coldness is a brand commitment.
options.kept: The one bright colour only on things you can press.

options.label: Reference Page
options.thesis: Two columns round a keyed centre rail.
options.case: Loses both axes: bookish for this audience.

options.label: Timetable Slides
options.thesis: One type size; rank by weight and case.
options.case: Loses both axes: too far from the audience.
options.kept: Text rank by weight and case, not size.

options.label: Mixtape Card
options.thesis: Ballpoint tracklists timed to fit a side.
options.case: Loses both axes: warm nostalgia, wrong generation.
options.kept: The day as a fixed budget quests must fit.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean Material 3 dark habit/fitness tracker, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, progress rings for the five domains, a checklist of quests, a labeled nav bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every habit tracker by design.
